Subject: Post-demo: regional inference routing, SLOs & data residency clarifications

Hi Sarah — thanks again for today’s demo and for walking through the core AVA workflows. Quick follow-up capturing the open items we discussed so we can align the PoC scope. Short bullets so we can turn this into a MAP: 

1) Latency targets (customer ask):
   - Primary: US (end users in US East) — target p95 generation latency <= 120ms for 512-token prompts
   - Secondary: EU — target p95 <= 180ms
   - APAC: pilot; acceptable p95 <= 300ms initially

2) Throughput / concurrency expectations:
   - Estimated steady-state: 80 requests/sec across service, burst to 220 req/sec for 10–15 min windows
   - Concurrent streams: up to 60 concurrent streaming sessions (low avg token/sec ~6)

3) Streaming and partial-response constraints:
   - Need sub-200ms first-token for streaming starts in US; token emission rate ~6 tokens/sec avg

4) Data residency / routing rules:
   - User data originating in EU must not leave EU region for inference or logged telemetry by default
   - US production traffic can stay in us-east region; APAC pilot can use us-west fallback if APAC capacity limited, but we understand this requires opt-in

5) Security/compliance ask (from your procurement): SOC2 report + data-flow diagram during PoC

Attached: demo-telemetry-snapshots.csv (sample p50/p90/p95 from our test cluster) and a short regional SLO proposal PDF.

Next steps I propose: 
- Karthik to confirm feasibility and any architectural notes (next email)
- We share a 4-week PoC MAP with milestones (integration, test traffic, SLA checks)
- Procurement: exchange SOC2 and initial contract terms

If that matches what you heard, I’ll turn this into a formal MAP and propose dates.

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
Enterprise Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Connor — very helpful summary, thanks. A couple clarifying Qs before we lock the MAP: 

1) APAC: when you say ‘pilot’ and fallback to US-west, can we require that no PII or logs leave APAC unless explicitly escalated? Our legal team needs a default 'no egress' posture for APAC user data.
2) Streaming: is the 200ms first-token realistic for 6 tokens/sec? Our UX team is sensitive to first-byte latency for chat.
3) Throughput: the 220 req/sec burst — do you recommend dedicated capacity for predictable SLAs or can we start on hosted and rely on fallback?

Procurement also wants to see the SOC2 report and a network/data-flow diagram showing exactly what telemetry Redwood retains during PoC. Can you include retention defaults and whether telemetry can be disabled?

We’re aiming to start the PoC in mid-September if we can get a MAP and SOC2 in the next 10 business days.

Sarah — quick tech notes and feasibility: quoting Connor’s bullets below for context.

> 1) Latency targets: US p95 <=120ms (512 tokens), EU p95 <=180ms, APAC p95 <=300ms
> 2) Throughput: steady 80 rps, burst 220 rps; concurrency 60 streaming sessions
> 3) Streaming first-token <200ms; token flow ~6 t/s
> 4) Data residency: EU traffic must stay in EU, APAC default no-egress

Feasibility & recommendations:
- US/EU strict residency: supported via region pinning. For EU-only workloads we deploy inference in eu-west cluster and disable cross-region failover by policy. That meets 'no egress' for inference and telemetry if you opt-in (we can provide a PoC config).
- APAC: we can run a lightweight on-prem appliance or private VPC in APAC to avoid egress. If that’s not an option initially, we recommend an explicit opt-in for APAC egress.
- Latency: p95 120ms for 512 tokens in US is achievable with a dedicated instance pool sized for your load (we can model). On hosted tiers with autoscale you may see higher tail latencies under bursts — for predictable p95 during bursts, preferred: reserved/dedicated capacity.
- Throughput/concurrency sizing: for 220 rps bursts and 60 concurrent streams, we'd recommend a pool of 8-10 cGPU-backed instances with continuous batching and streaming-optimized runtime; exact sizing depends on model size and quantization. We’ll run a capacity calc for your expected model (please share model or desired throughput per model).
- Streaming first-token: sub-200ms depends largely on network RTT + cold start. With warm workers in-region we routinely hit 80–150ms first-token for streaming; we’ll instrument for p50/p95 in the PoC and tune batch windows.
- Telemetry & retention: default telemetry collects aggregate latencies and error rates; raw request logging (inputs) is disabled by default. For PoC we can set retention to 7 days and provide an option to disable request-level logs. We will include a data-flow diagram and the SOC2 report in the next email.

Actionable asks for PoC prep (what we need from Ava):
- Confirm model(s) or us-to-run reference workload (sample payloads)
- Estimated traffic profile per region (RPS, concurrent streams) by hour/day
- Whether APAC will require on-prem/VPC option or can accept opt-in egress for pilot

I’ll follow up with a short regional sizing spreadsheet and suggested pool configs.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
